questions.question: The CPU and memory are located on the ___________ of the computer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**MotherBoard**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Motherboard:

 
 
• The motherboard serves as a single platform to connect all of the parts of a computer.
 
• It connects the CPU, memory, hard drives, optical drives, video cards, sound cards, and other ports and expansion cards directly or via cables.
 
• It can be considered the backbone of a computer.
 
• A motherboard comes with the following features −
 
 
• The **motherboard** varies greatly in supporting various types of components.
 
• The motherboard supports a single type of CPU and a few types of memory.
 
• Video cards, hard disks, and sound cards have to be compatible with the motherboard to function properly.
 
• Motherboards, cases, and power supplies must be compatible to work properly together.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• CPU:

 
 
• A Central Processing Unit is also called a processor, central processor, or microprocessor.
 
• It carries out all the important functions of a computer. It receives instructions from both the hardware and active software and produces output accordingly. It stores all important programs like operating systems and application software. 
 
• It is often referred to as the brain of the computer.

questions.question: In Gmail, what do you use when you receive mail and want to send the mail in response to the same mail and to the original sender only?
questions.solution:
**You should use the option "Reply" when you receive an email in Gmail and want to send a response to the original sender only.**

**Explanation:**

__
 
• "Reply" is the option you should choose when you want to respond to the original sender of an email only.
 
• When you click "Reply", Gmail will automatically populate the "To" field with the email address of the person who sent you the email.
 
• You can then type your response and send it directly to that person.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "Forward" is used to send an email to someone who was not originally included in the email thread. When you forward an email, you can add new recipients, modify the subject line or add additional comments.
 
• "Both Reply and Forward" is not an option in Gmail. However, you can reply to an email and then forward that reply to someone else.
 
• "Reply All" is used when you want to send a response to the original sender and all the other recipients of the original email. Use this option only when you want everyone on the email thread to see your response.

• Coal, which still dominates the energy mix, has fostered the development of industry and the **generation of electricity. **

• **Around 75% of the total power generated** is produced by coal-fired thermal power plants, which also produce the majority of electricity. The Central Electricity Authority said that **India generated 103.66 billion units of electricity** in December of 2020.

questions.question: How many types of white blood cells are there in human body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There are **5 types of white blood cells **__are there in the human body.
 
• Types of white blood cells are-
 __
 
• **Granulocytes (Eosinophils, Neutrophils, Basophils)**
 
 
• **Agranulocytes (Monocytes, Lymphocytes)**
 
 
 
 
 
• **WBC (White Blood Cells)**
 
 
• These are also called **leukocytes or leucocytes.**
 
• They are **cells of the immune system**, which is mainly responsible for protecting and fighting against invading pathogens.
 
• These cells stimulate the production of the progesterone hormone.
 
• They also play a vital role in the human reproductive system by producing a network of blood vessels within the ovary.
 
• On average, the total count of white blood cells in every microliter of blood ranges between 4 and 11 thousand, and a healthy person will produce around 80 to 100 billion white blood cells every day.
 
• **The lifespan of white blood cells ranges between 13 and 20 days.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Brief information on types of WBCs-
 
 
• **Eosinophils** are responsible for combating multicellular parasites and certain infections in vertebrates.
 
• **Neutrophils** form an essential part of the innate immune system, with their functions varying in different animals.
 
• **Basophils** release enzymes to improve blood flow and prevent blood clots.
 
• **Monocytes** play a role in both the inflammatory and anti-inflammatory processes that take place during an immune response.
 
• **Lymphocytes** help our body's immune system fight cancer and foreign viruses and bacteria.

questions.question:
In a balanced chemical reaction, like the one shown below, the values of a, b, c and d respectively, are:

a Fe + b H₂O → c Fe₃O₄ + d H₂
questions.solution:
The answer is __**3, 4, 1, 4.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Balancing Chemical Reaction:**

__
 
• The **given equation is**: a Fe + b H2O → c Fe3O4 + d H2.
 
• 
 
 
 

 **Reactant Side**
 **Product Side**
 
 

 1 Iron atom
 3 Iron atoms
 
 

 2 Hydrogen atoms 
 2 Hydrogen atoms
 
 

 1 Oxygen atom
 4 Oxygen atoms
 
 
 
 
 
• The **iron atoms are balanced** first. Once the equation is balanced, it becomes: **3Fe** + H2O → **Fe3**O4 + H2
 
• The **oxygen atoms are then balanced**. After the balancing the equation, it becomes: 3Fe + **4**H2**O **→ Fe3**O4** + H2
 
• At last, the **atoms of hydrogen are balanced**. Once the equation is balanced, it becomes: 3Fe + **4H2**O → Fe3O4 + **4H2**
 
• The balanced chemical reaction is: **3 Fe + 4 H2O → 1 Fe3O4 + 4 H2.**
 
• 
 
 
 

 Reactant Side
 Product Side
 
 

 3 Iron atoms
 3 Iron atoms
 
 

 8 Hydrogen atoms 
 8 Hydrogen atoms
 
 

 4 Oxygen atom
 4 Oxygen atoms
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Balanced Chemical Reaction:**

 
• It is a chemical equation that represents the **conservation of mass and charge** in a chemical reaction.
 
• The number of atoms of **each element and the total charge on both reactant and product sides of the equation must be equal.**
 
• It is important to balance chemical reactions to **understand the stoichiometry of the reaction and predict the amount of reactants and products** formed.
 
• The **oxygen and hydrogen atoms' stoichiometric coefficients** are typically **assigned last.**

questions.question: The term 'geography' was coined by who among the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eratosthenes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Eratosthenes was a Greek mathematician, geographer, poet, astronomer, and music theorist.
 
• He is best known for being the first person to use the term 'geography' and for his work in geography, particularly his calculation of the Earth's circumference.
 
• He was the chief librarian at the Library of Alexandria.
 
• Eratosthenes created one of the earliest maps of the world and introduced the concept of latitude and longitude.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eratosthenes' Contributions to Geography**

 
 
• Eratosthenes is often referred to as the 'Father of Geography' for his significant contributions to the field.
 
• He invented the discipline of geography, including the terminology we still use today.
 
• One of his most famous achievements was calculating the circumference of the Earth with remarkable accuracy for his time.
 
• He also created a system of latitude and longitude, which laid the foundation for modern cartography and navigation.
 
 
 
• **Al Idrisi**
 
 
• Al Idrisi was an Arab Muslim geographer, cartographer, and Egyptologist who lived in the 12th century.
 
• He is best known for his work "Tabula Rogeriana," which is one of the most advanced medieval world maps.
 
• His work was highly influential in the medieval Islamic world and in Europe.
 
 
 
• **Ptolemy**
 
 
• Ptolemy was a Greco-Egyptian writer of Alexandria, known for his work in astronomy, mathematics, and geography.
 
• He authored the "Geographia," a comprehensive treatise on the geographical knowledge of the Greco-Roman world.
 
• Ptolemy's work influenced geographic thought for over a thousand years.
 
 
 
• **Carl Ritter**
 
 
• Carl Ritter was a German geographer who is considered one of the founders of modern geography.
 
• He emphasized the importance of empirical observation and the interrelation between human and physical geography.
 
• His work laid the groundwork for future geographical studies and education.

questions.question: Seismograph is used to measure:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Earthquakes**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plate Tectonics**:

 
 
• Seismographs can provide indirect evidence supporting the theory of plate tectonics.
 
• By recording earthquake patterns and magnitudes around the world, they help illustrate the world’s tectonic plate boundaries where earthquakes are common.
 
 
 
• **Epicenter and Focus of Earthquakes**:
 
 
• Seismographs play a crucial role in locating the epicenter (geographical location directly above the focus on the surface) and the focus (actual location within the earth where the earthquake originates) of an earthquake.
 
• Data collected from minimum three seismograph stations is used to triangulate the epicenter of an earthquake.
 
 
 
• **Seismic Wave Speed Variations**:
 
 
• P-waves (primary waves) and S-waves (secondary waves) recorded by seismographs travel at different speeds and through different parts of the Earth's interior.
 
• Based on their arrival times at seismograph stations, we can infer properties of the Earth's interior, such as the presence of a molten outer core (which S-waves cannot travel through).
 
 
 
• **Seismicities**:
 
 
• Analysis of seismographs can help identify areas known as seismicities - geographical zones with a high frequency of earthquakes.
 
• Historical data from seismographs can therefore be used to predict regions where future earthquakes may occur.
 
 
 
• **Earth's Interior Structure**:
 
 
• Seismograph readings help scientists understand the Earth's interior structure better.
 
• For instance, changes in seismic wave velocity indicate interfaces between different layers of the Earth's interior, such as the crust, mantle, and core.
 
 
 
• **Human-Induced Seismic Activity**:
 
 
• Seismographs not only capture natural seismic activity, but also man-made seismic events such as those resulting from mining, reservoir-induced seismicity, nuclear tests, and construction work.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Earthquake Waves**:

 
• Earthquake waves are vibrations in the Earth's crust caused by seismic events like earthquakes or volcanic activity.
 
• Two main types: body waves and surface waves.

**Body Waves**:

 
• Generated at the earthquake's focus and travel in all directions through the Earth's interior.
 
• Interact with surface rocks, generating surface waves.
 
• Changes in velocity and direction due to material density differences.
 
• **Two types**: P-waves (primary waves) and S-waves (secondary waves).

**P-Waves (Primary Waves)**: 

 
• Fastest seismic waves, reaching the surface first.
 
• Similar to sound waves, they travel through gaseous, liquid, and solid materials.
 
• Provide important information about the Earth's interior structure.

**S-Waves (Secondary Waves)**:

 
• Arrive at the surface after P-waves.
 
• Can only travel through solid materials, not liquids or gases.
 
• Vital for understanding the Earth's interior composition and structure.

**Surface Waves**:

 
• ​Generated by interaction between body waves and surface rocks.
 
• Slowest seismic waves, causing significant damage.
 
• Displace rocks and contribute to structural collapses.

questions.question: Which of the following industries generates invisible exports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tourism**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** tourism industry generates invisible exports**
 
• **Invisible exports are a part of international trade **that doesn't involve the exchange of physical goods or tangible objects.
 
• Tourism is **considered an invisible export because it involves financial transactions without the exchange of physical goods.**

questions.question: What type of bonding is present in carbon compounds?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Covalent Bonding**.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Carbon forms** covalent bonds.
 
• There are **three major types of covalent bonds:** single, double, and triple bonds.
 
• **A carbon atom can form four single bonds.**
 
• A Covalent bond is a bond that is formed after the sharing of electron pairs between atoms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Metallic Bonding:**

 
 
• **Metallic bonding occurs when metal atoms share their valence electrons freely in a "sea of electrons." **
 
• This bonding explains the properties of metals such as electrical conductivity, malleability, and ductility.
 
• **Example: Copper (Cu)**
 
• Copper atoms bond together with metallic bonds, allowing electrons to move freely, giving copper its excellent electrical conductivity.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Bonding:**
 
 
• **Hydrogen bonding occurs when hydrogen is covalently bonded to a highly electronegative element like nitrogen, oxygen, or fluorine,** and is attracted to a lone pair of electrons on another electronegative atom.
 
• **Example: Water (H₂O)**
 
• In water, hydrogen bonds form between the hydrogen atoms of one molecule and the oxygen atom of another, giving water its high boiling point and surface tension.
 
 
 
• **Ionic Bonding:**
 
 
• Ionic bonding** occurs when one atom donates an electron to another, creating positively and negatively charged ions that are attracted to each other.**
 
• **Example: Sodium chloride (NaCl)**
 
• Sodium (Na) donates an electron to chlorine (Cl), forming Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions that are held together by electrostatic forces.

questions.question: _______ are rules that exist at several levels in a telecommunication connection.
questions.solution:
__
 
• Protocol are rules that exist at several levels in a telecommunication connection.
 
• Protocols are a set of rules and standards that govern how data is transmitted between devices in a network.
 
• They define the format, timing, sequencing, and error checking of data transmitted over a network, and enable devices from different manufacturers to communicate with each other. Examples of common protocols include TCP/IP, HTTP, FTP, SMTP, and DNS.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Bandwidth: Bandwidth refers to the amount of data that can be transmitted over a communication channel in a given amount of time.
 
• It is typically measured in bits per second (bps) or bytes per second (Bps).
 
• Bandwidth is an important factor in determining the speed and capacity of a network, and it is affected by factors such as the type of transmission medium, the number of users on the network, and the quality of the signal.
 
• Network Surface Unit: It's possible that you meant "Network Interface Unit" or "Network Interface Card" (NIC), which is a hardware component that allows a device to connect to a network.
 
• A NIC typically provides a physical interface (such as an Ethernet port) for connecting to the network, as well as the necessary drivers and software for controlling the connection.
 
• Domain Name: A domain name is a unique identifier for a website or other internet resource.
 
• It typically consists of two parts: a top-level domain (TLD), such as .com, .org, or .edu, and a second-level domain (SLD), which is the specific name chosen by the owner of the domain.
 
• Domain names are used to make it easier for users to find and access websites, and they are managed by domain name registrars and domain name system (DNS) servers.

questions.question: What type of memory is used to store data temporarily while a computer is running?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**RAM**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory)** is a **volatile memory **used to temporarily store data while a computer is running.
 
• It facilitates quick access to data for the processor, enabling smooth execution of programs and tasks.
 
• The data stored in RAM is cleared when the computer is powered off, making it ideal for temporary storage.
 
• RAM enhances the performance of a computer by allowing faster read and write operations compared to storage devices like hard disks or SSDs.
 
• Modern computers typically use DDR (Double Data Rate) RAM, such as DDR4 or DDR5, for improved speed and efficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Volatile Memory:** Volatile memory loses its content when the power is turned off. RAM is an example of volatile memory.
 
• **Non-volatile Memory:** Non-volatile memory retains data even when the computer is powered off. Examples include hard drives, SSDs, and ROM.
 
• **Cache Memory:** Cache is a smaller, faster type of memory located inside or close to the CPU, used to store frequently accessed data for quicker retrieval.
 
• **Hard Disk:** A hard disk is a non-volatile storage device used to store permanent data such as files, applications, and the operating system.
 
• **ROM (Read-Only Memory):** ROM is a type of non-volatile memory that contains essential instructions for booting up the computer and cannot be modified easily.

questions.question: 'Edema' is related with ____________
questions.solution:
**__Concept __:**

**Lymphatic system :**

__
 
• When the blood passes through the capillaries in tissues, some water along with many small water-soluble substances move out into the spaces between the cells of tissues leaving the larger proteins in the blood vessels.
 
• This fluid released out is called the tissue fluid.
 
• The exchange of nutrients, gases, etc., between the blood and the cells, always occurs through this fluid.
 
• An elaborate network of vessels called the** lymphatic system **collects this fluid and drains it back to the major veins.
 
• The fluid present in the lymphatic system is called** lymph.**
 
• Lymph is a **colorless fluid **containing specialized lymphocytes which are responsible for the** immune responses **of the body.
 
• The lymph is also an important carrier of nutrients, hormones, etc.** **

**Explanation__ :**

__
 
• **Edema **is a condition in which body parts** swell **due to the** accumulation of fluids in the tissues.**
 
• **Lymphedema** is an ailment in which there is an accumulation of fluid that is usually drained through the lymphatic system.
 
• It can lead to skin and tissue changes.
 
• Most commonly affected parts are **the arms or legs**, but can also occur in the chest wall, abdomen, neck, and genitals.

**So, the correct answer is the Lymphatic system.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The most common treatment for lymphedema is complete decongestive therapy.
 
• It involves a comprehensive combination of skincare, compressive bandaging, exercise, and a form of massage called manual lymph drainage.

questions.question: Which bacteria is found in roots of leguminous plants as symbionts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rhizobium**__.

__**Concept:**__

__
 
• **Microorganisms **are too small and are not visible to naked eyes.
 
• Microorganisms are found in air, water and in the bodies of plants and animals.
 
• They may be **unicellular **or **multicellular**.
 
• Microorganisms are classified into **four major groups**.
 
 
• **Bacteria**- Bacteria convert gaseous nitrogen into a usable form and release it into the soil.
 
• **Fungi**- Fungi are cosmopolitan and occur in air, water, soil and on animals and plants.
 
• **Protozoa**- protozoans are heterotrophs and live as predators or parasites.
 
• **Algae**- Algae are largely aquatic both fresh water and marine organisms.
 
 

**Explanation:**__

__
 
• **Leguminous plants belong to the family Fabaceae.**
 
• These **plants have a symbiotic relationship with the soil bacteria** Rhizobium, which lives in their roots.
 
• **Rhizobium **is a **biofertiliser**. 
 
• Biofertilizers are the microorganisms that enrich the nutrient (nitrogen, phosphorous, etc.) quality of the soil.
 
• **Rhizobium is a** **symbiotic bacterium that lives in the root nodules of leguminous ****plants**__ and **fixes atmospheric nitrogen into organic compound** (ammonia) and it also fertilizes the soil.
 
• It causes the formation of special structures known as **nodules **within the cell, which fix atmospheric nitrogen.
 
• It accomplishes this with the help of the nitrogenase enzyme, which converts nitrogen to ammonium, a necessary factor for plant growth.
 
• Rhizobium bacteria form symbiotic associations with plants.
 
• **Plants provide them with food and shelter**, and these bacteria fix nitrogen in the soil.

questions.question: In Kheda, Gujarat, Patidar peasants organised non-violent campaigns against which of the following demand of the British?

• This was** one of the key issues that led to the Kheda Satyagraha of 1918, **a significant event in the **Indian independence movement, which was led by figures like Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, Vallabhbhai Patel, and others.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Kheda Satyagraha__

 
 
• In the middle of the Kheda Satyagraha (1918), Gandhi also got involved in the Ahmedabad textile mill strike.
 
• Here his adversaries were the Gujarati millowners.
 
• The immediate reason for the industrial conflict was the withdrawal of plague bonus, which was being given to dissuade workers from leaving the city in the face of mounting plague-related deaths.
 
• Also, it was during Ahmedabad textile mill strike that Gandhiji for the first time during the Indian National Movement took fast unto death( to strengthen the workers‘ resolve).
 
• Hence his first hunger strike was during Ahmedabad Strike and not at Kheda.
 
• The cause for Kheda Satyagraha was that the peasants of Kheda district were in extreme distress due to a failure of crops and that their appeals for the remission of land revenue were being ignored by the Government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Trilateral Summit 2025** was a high-level meeting involving three major international organizations: **WHO (World Health Organization)**, **WIPO (World Intellectual Property Organization)**, and **WTO (World Trade Organization)**.
 
• The summit was held in **Geneva, Switzerland**, which serves as the headquarters for these organizations.
 
• The summit aimed to enhance cooperation between global health, intellectual property, and trade bodies to address contemporary challenges.
 
• Discussions focused on improving access to medicines, innovation, and equitable trade policies worldwide.
 
• Geneva's role as a diplomatic hub makes it a frequent venue for important international summits and negotiations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The WHO, WIPO, and WTO are all specialized agencies of the United Nations system based in Geneva.
 
• Geneva has been a long-standing center for international diplomacy, hosting multiple UN agencies and international organizations.
 
• The summit symbolizes the increasing interconnection of health, trade, and intellectual property in global governance.
 
• It reflects ongoing efforts to streamline policies and frameworks among the three organizations to better tackle global issues.
